title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants: Chapter Introduction
subject: Biology
objective: A flower is a plant's reproductive organ. Pollen reaches the stigma, a pollen tube delivers two male gametes, double fertilisation follows, and the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary a fruit.

fill.q: Pollen grains are formed in the ____ of the stamen.
The part of the pistil that receives pollen is the ____.
The pollen tube carries ____ male gametes into the ovule.
Fusion of a male gamete with the two polar nuclei is called ____ fusion.
After fertilisation the ovule develops into the ____.

tf.q: The stamen is the female reproductive part of a flower.
tf.explain: The stamen is male; the pistil is female.

tf.q: Insects, wind and water can all be agents of pollination.
tf.explain: These carry pollen to the stigma.
The zygote is diploid (2n); the primary endosperm nucleus is triploid (3n).

tf.q: After fertilisation the ovary becomes the fruit.

ar.a: Double fertilisation gives both a zygote and an endosperm.
ar.r: One male gamete fuses with the egg and the other with the two polar nuclei.
ar.explain: R describes the two fusions in A.

ar.a: A mango is a ripened ovary.
ar.r: After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit.

mcq.q: The female reproductive part of a flower is the:

mcq.explain: One male gamete (n) + two polar nuclei (n + n) = 3n.

mcq.q: Formation of seeds without fertilisation is called:

num.q: If a plant's egg cell has 12 chromosomes, how many are in its zygote and its primary endosperm nucleus?
A flower has 5 ovules, each fertilised. How many male gametes and how many pollen tubes are needed?
steps: Each ovule needs one pollen tube

short.solution: The pollen tube releases two male gametes into the embryo sac. One fuses with the egg (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote; the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

short.q: What happens to the ovule and the ovary after fertilisation?
short.solution: The ovule develops into the seed (zygote → embryo, PEN → endosperm) and the ovary develops into the fruit.

match.explain: Each structure matches its role in reproduction.
